from.place: Integral exceptional-adjoint proof, paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation; technical foundations for the finite-adjunction-diagram realization, specifically the full functor-category pushout comparison in lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization. Technical input: Strict simplicial-model diagrams and coherent cone mapping spaces.

title: Strict simplicial-model diagrams and coherent cone mapping spaces
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories, mapping spaces, cones and cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the homotopy coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ and coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], in nested universes large enough for the collections below. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category. This means a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category with functorial model factorizations generated by sets, enriched, tensored and cotensored over simplicial sets with the Kan model structure and satisfying the simplicial pushout-product axiom. The Kan model structure has degreewise monomorphisms as cofibrations, weak homotopy equivalences as weak equivalences, and maps with the right lifting property against all horn inclusions as fibrations. The simplicial pushout-product axiom says that the pushout product of a cofibration of $\mathcal M$ and a cofibration of simplicial sets is a cofibration of $\mathcal M$, trivial if either factor is trivial; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Model factorizations mean retract-closed weak equivalences $W$ with two-out-of-three and weak factorization systems (cofibrations, fibrations in $W$) and (cofibrations in $W$, fibrations), where each pair consists of mutually characterized diagonal-lifting classes and every arrow factors through them. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated, for some regular cardinal $\kappa$, under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits. An object is cofibrant if its initial map is a cofibration, fibrant if its terminal map is a fibration. Let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}}$ be its simplicial subcategory of cofibrant-fibrant objects and put $\mathcal C=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}})$.

Let $K$ be a small simplicial set and $u:\mathfrak C[K]\to I$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence to a small fibrant simplicial category $I$. Dwyer--Kan equivalence means equivalence on the categories of components and weak homotopy equivalence on all mapping simplicial sets; fibrant here means that all mapping simplicial sets are Kan. Such an $I$ may be obtained by fibrant replacement of $\mathfrak C[K]$. The category $\mathcal M^I$ of simplicial enriched functors has projective and injective simplicial model structures, both with objectwise weak equivalences; projective fibrations and injective cofibrations are objectwise. For an object $i$ of $I$ and $A\in\mathcal M$, the free diagram $F_i(A)$ has value $I(i,j)\otimes A$ at $j$. Given a set $J$ of generating cofibrations of $\mathcal M$, the maps $F_i(a)\to F_i(b)$, for $(a\to b)\in J$, generate the projective cofibrations: every projective cofibration is a retract of a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of these maps. Restriction along $u$ and the coherent-nerve adjunction give a natural equivalence
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}((\mathcal M^I)^{\mathrm{cf}})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C),$$
using either model structure. In particular every coherent $K$-diagram has such a strict enriched presentation, including its transformation spaces.

Let $F:I\to\mathcal M$ present $p:K\to\mathcal C$. Let $QF$ be a projectively cofibrant replacement and $TF$ an injectively fibrant replacement. Write $\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{enr}}_I$ and $\operatorname{lim}^{\mathrm{enr}}_I$ for the enriched conical (co)limits, characterized by the enriched adjunctions with the constant-diagram functor; these exist since $\mathcal M$ is complete, cocomplete, tensored and cotensored. After cofibrant-fibrant replacement of their apices, put $L=R\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{enr}}_I QF$ and $H=Q\operatorname{lim}^{\mathrm{enr}}_I TF$. Here $R$ is fibrant replacement of the already cofibrant colimit and $Q$ is cofibrant replacement of the already fibrant limit. For every $Y\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}}$, the adjunction maps induce natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(L,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(p,\Delta_KY),\qquad
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Y,H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(\Delta_KY,p).$$
These equivalences identify the canonical cocone and cone. All constructions are relative to the universe of $K,I$ and the model objects involved.

If every object of $\mathcal M$ is cofibrant, then for a cospan of fibrant objects $X\to Z\leftarrow Y$ in $\mathcal M$, choose a path object $Z\xrightarrow{\sim}V\twoheadrightarrow Z\times Z$ (a weak equivalence followed by a fibration factoring the diagonal). The strict pullback $X\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}V\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}Y$, with its induced cone, represents the homotopy pullback of the associated cospan in $\mathcal C$. This is the cospan instance of the cone comparison above; no right properness is required because all three objects are fibrant.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5 (enriched projective and injective model structures, their simplicial compatibility and free-diagram generating cofibrations), Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5 (rectification), Theorem 4.2.4.1 (homotopy-(co)limit comparison), and the construction in Corollary 4.2.4.8. The displayed mapping-space formulas spell out the enriched adjunction computation underlying these results. The last path-object computation is the fibrant-cospan homotopy-limit construction of Proposition A.2.4.4 and Remark A.2.4.5 (fibrant-object alternative to right properness). Read online 2026-10-16; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] to the given $\mathcal M,I$. It supplies a locally presentable diagram category, objectwise ordinary limits and colimits, objectwise tensors and cotensors, and the enriched natural-transformation mapping sets. In particular its free-evaluation adjunction is $F_i(A)_j=I(i,j)\otimes A$. For every simplicial set $T$, the map $\varnothing\to T$ is a cofibration, by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The pushout-product axiom therefore says that $T\otimes-$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Consequently each free image of a ground (trivial) cofibration is objectwise of that kind.

source.place: A.3.3.3 and Remark A.3.3.5; simplicial sets are all cofibrant.

proof.text: Choose generating cofibrations $J$ and generating trivial cofibrations $J_t$ of $\mathcal M$. Let $S=\{F_i(a):i\in I,\ a\in J\}$ and $S_t=\{F_i(a):i\in I,\ a\in J_t\}$, and write $W_I$ for objectwise weak equivalences. The adjunction of step 1 identifies $S^\perp$ with objectwise trivial fibrations and $S_t^\perp$ with objectwise fibrations. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-small-object-factorization] to the locally presentable diagram category and each of these small sets. This gives functorial factorizations with left classes $C_p={}^\perp(S^\perp)$ and $T_p={}^\perp(S_t^\perp)$. For either set, [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] also gives a factorization with cellular left factor. A map in its left lifting class lifts against the right factor, hence is a retract of that cellular left factor. Conversely cells have the left lifting property: extend a lift successively across each attached generator, use the colimit at a limit ordinal, and pass to retracts. This proves both the weak factorization systems and the retract-of-cells description. By step 1 and objectwise colimits, every map in $C_p$ is an objectwise cofibration and every map in $T_p$ is an objectwise trivial cofibration. Also $S_t\subseteq C_p$, since each ground trivial cofibration lifts against each ground trivial fibration, so $T_p\subseteq C_p\cap W_I$. If $f\in C_p\cap W_I$, factor it as $f=pj$, $j\in T_p$, $p$ an objectwise fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $p$ an objectwise trivial fibration. The lifting property of $f$ against $p$ exhibits $f$ as a retract of $j$, so $C_p\cap W_I=T_p$. The two weak factorization systems therefore satisfy the model axioms. Objectwise weak equivalences have retract closure and two-out-of-three, and both systems are set-generated, giving the combinatorial projective structure and the asserted generating cofibrations. The same cellular-factorization and retract argument applied in the ground category shows that its cofibrations and trivial cofibrations are the respective weakly saturated closures of $J$ and $J_t$; this is the ground generation assertion used in Step 3.

source.place: HTT A.1.2.5, A.1.2.7, proof of A.2.8.2 (projective case), A.3.3.2-A.3.3.5; explicit lifting and retract calculations.

proof.text: Let $C_i$ be the objectwise cofibrations and $W_I$ the objectwise weak equivalences. The small-generation clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation], applied to a ground generating set of cofibrations, gives a small generating set for $C_i$. Apply its same clause to the ground generating trivial cofibrations: $C_i\cap W_I$ is weakly saturated. By [lem-coef-model-weak-equivalences-accessible] the ground weak equivalences form an accessible, accessibly embedded full subcategory of the arrow category. The pointwise accessibility clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] gives this property for $W_I$. Retract closure, repleteness and two-out-of-three hold componentwise. Finally $C_i^{\square}\subseteq S^{\square}\subseteq W_I$, because Step 1 puts the free generating cofibrations $S$ inside $C_i$, and Step 2 identifies $S^{\square}$ with objectwise trivial fibrations. All five hypotheses of [lem-coef-smith-model-recognition] now hold for the locally presentable diagram category. It gives a combinatorial injective model structure with cofibrations $C_i$, weak equivalences $W_I$, fibrations $(C_i\cap W_I)^{\square}$ and functorial factorizations.

source.place: Proof of A.2.8.2, injective case; Lemma A.3.3.3 and Proposition A.2.6.10.

proof.text: Both structures satisfy the simplicial axiom. For the injective structure, the pushout product of a diagram cofibration $f$ with a simplicial cofibration $j$ is objectwise $f_i\mathbin{\square}j$, and so is an injective cofibration, trivial if either input is trivial, by the ground axiom. For the projective structure it suffices to check the generating cofibrations and generating trivial cofibrations from step 2: the identities $F_i(a)\mathbin{\square}j=F_i(a\mathbin{\square}j)$ follow from the tensor adjunction and the associativity of the tensor. Free-evaluation adjunctions and objectwise (trivial) fibrations make the latter maps projective (trivial) cofibrations. Pushout product preserves coproducts, pushouts, transfinite composition, and retracts in each variable, so the generating-cell description proves the assertion for every projective cofibration, and likewise for every projective trivial cofibration. Thus the enriched natural-transformation mapping sets from step 1 are the simplicial model enrichments of both structures.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.4; generating-cell verification using steps 1-3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification] with its comparison target $\mathcal C$ equal to the present $I$, its indexing simplicial set equal to $K$, and the given $u:\mathfrak C[K]\to I$. Its combinatorial and simplicial projective-model hypotheses have been checked in steps 1-4. Write $P$ and $Q$ for the full simplicial subcategories of $\mathcal M^I$ on projectively, respectively injectively, bifibrant diagrams. The cited node gives the asserted projective comparison $e_p:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(P)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, including transformation spaces, by enriched evaluation and $u$. Injectively cofibrant diagrams are objectwise cofibrant by definition. An injectively fibrant diagram is objectwise fibrant: each free image of a ground trivial cofibration is an objectwise trivial cofibration by Step 1, hence an injective trivial cofibration, and the free-evaluation adjunction converts lifting against it to the ground fibrancy lifting test at that vertex. Projective cofibrations are objectwise cofibrations and projective fibrancy is objectwise by step 2. Hence every object of $P$ and of $Q$ lies in the full simplicial subcategory $E$ of objectwise bifibrant diagrams. Enriched evaluation is a simplicial functor $I\times E\to\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}}$, so the coherent-nerve adjunction and $u$ give one simplicial map $e:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, whose restrictions are $e_p$ and the injective comparison $e_q$. By step 4 both diagram structures are simplicial model categories, so [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] applies to each. They have the same underlying category $\mathcal M^I$ and the same weak equivalences $W_I$, hence one localization $\mathcal L$. That node gives equivalences $\psi_p:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(P)\to\mathcal L$ and $\psi_q:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Q)\to\mathcal L$ whose restrictions to the ordinary nerves $N(P_0)$, $N(Q_0)$ are inclusion followed by localization; by its bifibrant-subcategory clause, $N(Q_0)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Q)$ is therefore an infinity localization at $W_I$. Put $\Phi=\psi_p^{-1}\psi_q$. For $G\in Q$ let $c_G:Q_pG\to G$ be the functorial projective cofibrant replacement of step 2, a projective trivial fibration, i.e. objectwise a trivial fibration. Since $G$ is objectwise fibrant, so is $Q_pG$; thus $Q_pG\in P$ and $Q_p$ is an ordinary functor $Q_0\to P_0$. The maps $c_G$ become equivalences in $\mathcal L$, so $\psi_p$ restricted along $N(Q_p)$ is naturally equivalent to $\psi_q$ on $N(Q_0)$, i.e. $\Phi|_{N(Q_0)}$ is naturally equivalent to $N(Q_p)$ followed by $N(P_0)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(P)$. The same maps $c_G$ are natural edges of $N(E_0)\subseteq N_{\mathrm{hc}}(E)$, so $e$ carries them to a coherent transformation $e_p\circ N(Q_p)\Rightarrow e_q|_{N(Q_0)}$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(N(Q_0)\times K,\mathcal C)$. Its vertex components are the maps $(c_G)_{u(k)}$, weak equivalences between bifibrant objects of $\mathcal M$, hence equivalences of $\mathcal C$ by the localization; by the vertex criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it is a natural equivalence. Thus $e_p\Phi$ and $e_q$ have naturally equivalent restrictions to $N(Q_0)$. Both invert $W_I$, and restriction along the localization $N(Q_0)\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Q)$ is fully faithful on such functors, so $e_q\simeq e_p\Phi$, an equivalence. Finally, for $Y\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}}$ the constant diagram $\Delta_IY$ lies in $E$ with $e(\Delta_IY)=\Delta_KY$, and its projective cofibrant and injective fibrant replacements are joined to it by objectwise weak equivalences, which $e$ sends to equivalences by the same vertex criterion. So both comparisons identify localized constant diagrams with $\Delta_K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5; the common localization identifies the injective comparison with the projective one through functorial projective cofibrant replacement.

proof.text: Using the objectwise enrichment, tensors, cotensors, limits and colimits supplied by [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation], make the following explicit constructions. The enriched conical colimit is the coequalizer of the action and augmentation maps $\coprod_{i,j}I(i,j)\otimes F_i\rightrightarrows\coprod_iF_i$: one map uses the diagram action and the other $I(i,j)\to\Delta^0$ followed by inclusion of $F_i$. A map from this coequalizer to $Y$, in any simplicial degree, is precisely a family $F_i\otimes\Delta^n\to Y$ compatible with those actions in degree $n$. Dually the enriched conical limit is the equalizer $\prod_iF_i\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F_j^{I(i,j)}$, the maps being the $i$-action map and the constant map from the $j$-factor. Its maps from $Y$ are exactly compatible families $Y\to F_i$. Tensors are left adjoints and cotensors right adjoints, so these descriptions hold in every simplicial degree. Thus they give the two enriched adjunctions with constants. In the projective structure constants preserve fibrations and trivial fibrations, since they are objectwise; consequently colimit preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations by adjunction of lifting squares. In the injective structure constants preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, so limit preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. In particular $A=\operatorname{colim}^{\mathrm{enr}}QF$ is cofibrant and $B=\operatorname{lim}^{\mathrm{enr}}TF$ is fibrant.

source.place: A.3.3.7 for the functor to the one-object simplicial category; explicit coequalizer/equalizer and lifting-square arguments from steps 1-4.

proof.text:
For $Y$ bifibrant, $\Delta_IY$ is projectively fibrant and $QF$ projectively cofibrant. The mapping-space clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], first for $\mathcal M$ and then for its projective diagram model, and the enriched adjunction of step 6 give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(RA,Y)\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(A,Y)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M^I}(QF,\Delta_IY)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(p,\Delta_KY).$$
The first equivalence uses $A\to RA$ in the localization and cofibrancy of $A$, so it needs no cofibrant-domain hypothesis on the ground generating maps. In the injective model $\Delta_IY$ is cofibrant and $TF$ fibrant. The same cited mapping-space clause and the other enriched adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Y,QB)\simeq\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(Y,B)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M^I}(\Delta_IY,TF)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(\Delta_KY,p).$$
The replacement $QB\to B$ identifies the two apices in the localization. Step 5 provides the last equivalences in both formulas. Naturality follows from the enriched adjunctions and the natural mapping-space identifications of the cited node.

source.place: The enriched-adjunction calculation behind Theorem 4.2.4.1 and Corollary 4.2.4.8; no derived-adjunction black box.

proof.text: Under the enriched colimit adjunction the identity of $A$ corresponds to the actual cocone $QF\to\Delta_IA$, and under the limit adjunction the identity of $B$ corresponds to $\Delta_IB\to TF$. Compose the first with $A\to RA$ and invert $QF\to F$ in the localized diagram category; for the second precompose with $QB\to B$ and invert $F\to TF$. Thus the maps of Step 7 are exactly composition with these localized cocone and cone transformations, not merely some equivalence of mapping spaces. The comparison of step 5 respects evaluation and coherent compositions. The criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore makes these cocones colimiting and cones limiting, with their specified transformations. This proves the canonical-(co)cone assertions, including for empty $K$.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.4.1 and Corollary 4.2.4.8; explicit unit/counit identification.

proof.text: For the final clause assume all objects are cofibrant and put $s:Z\to V$ for the path-object weak equivalence. Since $Z$ is fibrant, each $e_a:V\to Z$ is a fibration (compose $V\to Z^2$ with the fibrant product projection), and $e_as=1_Z$ makes it a trivial fibration. Put $X'=X\times_{Z,e_0}V$, with map $f'=e_1\operatorname{pr}_V$ to $Z$. Its projection to $X$ is a trivial fibration; its section $x\mapsto(x,sf(x))$ is a weak equivalence, and $f'$ is a fibration since $X'\to X\times Z$ is a pullback of $V\to Z^2$ and $X$ is fibrant. Put $Y'=Y\times_{Z,e_0}V$ and $g'=e_1\operatorname{pr}_V$. The projection $Y'\to Y$ is a pullback of the trivial fibration $e_0$, and its section $y\mapsto(y,sg(y))$ is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. The map $Y'\to Y\times Z$ is a pullback of $V\to Z^2$, and $Y\times Z\to Z$ is a fibration because $Y$ is fibrant. Thus $g'$ is a fibration. Thus $X',Y',V$ are fibrant. The cospan $X'\to Z\leftarrow Y'$ is injectively fibrant: to lift an objectwise trivial cofibration of cospan diagrams against it, first lift at $Z$ using fibrancy of $Z$, then lift at $X'$ and $Y'$ over this chosen lift using the fibrations $f',g'$. The sections define an objectwise weak equivalence from the original cospan to this injectively fibrant diagram. Its strict limit $P'=X'\times_ZY'$ therefore represents the coherent pullback by steps 5-8, using the discrete simplicial cospan category. This is permitted in the comparison because the counit $\mathfrak C[N(I)]\to I$ for that locally Kan discrete category is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification].

source.place: Proposition A.2.4.4 and Remark A.2.4.5, with an explicit injectively fibrant cospan replacement.

proof.text: The displayed object in the statement is $P=X'\times_ZY$. The section $Y\to Y'$ induces $h:P\to P'$. Both are fibrant: their maps to $Y,Y'$ respectively are pullbacks of the fibration $f'$. For every bifibrant $T$, enriched Hom preserves these pullbacks and sends $f'$ to a Kan fibration by the simplicial axiom. It also sends a weak equivalence $a:U\to U'$ between fibrant objects to a weak homotopy equivalence, as follows directly from the model axioms: factor $(1_U,a):U\to U\times U'$ as a trivial cofibration $i:U\to D$ and a fibration $(r,t):D\to U\times U'$. Then $r,t$ are fibrations, $ri=1$, $ti=a$, and two-out-of-three makes $r,t$ trivial fibrations. The simplicial axiom makes both maps $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,r)$ and $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,t)$ trivial Kan fibrations, and the section identity makes $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,i)$ a weak homotopy equivalence. Apply this to $Y\to Y'$. The square on mapping spaces induced by $h$ is its pullback along the Kan fibration $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,P')\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,Y')$. Right properness of Kan complexes in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,h)$ a weak homotopy equivalence. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] these are the actual mapping spaces of $\mathcal C$. This detects that $h$ is an equivalence: taking $T=P'$ gives a right inverse up to homotopy, and taking $T=P$ and injectivity on components gives the other inverse equation. Here $P,P'$ are bifibrant because all objects were assumed cofibrant. For an arbitrary path object, specify the coherent cone in the localization. Because $s$ is an equivalence, precomposition with $s$ gives an equivalence of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(V,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(Z,Z)$: precomposition with a coherent inverse gives its inverse, with the inverse equations supplied by coherent composition. The homotopy fiber over $1_Z$ is therefore contractible. The equalities $e_0s=e_1s=1_Z$ specify two points of this fiber, and a path between them gives a coherent homotopy $e_0\simeq e_1$ together with its restriction along $s$ identified with the constant homotopy. These are homotopy-fiber data, not an assertion that an arbitrary strict path object has a preferred literal interval map. Pull this homotopy back along the $V$-coordinate of $X'$ to identify the two composites $P\to X\to Z$ and $P\to Y\to Z$. This is the induced coherent cone on $P$. The limiting cone on $P'$ is the strict cone to the replacement cospan followed by the inverses of its two section equivalences. On restricting along $h$, the $Y'$-coordinate is the section at $Y$, so its resulting homotopy is constant; the $X'$-coordinate gives precisely the just-specified homotopy. Thus $h$ is a comparison of cones over the original cospan. Consequently $h$ identifies the induced coherent cone on $P$ with the limiting cone on $P'$; equivalence on the apex preserves the mapping-space criterion of step 8. Hence the single-path pullback $P$ represents the required coherent pullback. Only Kan-complex right properness was used.

source.place: A.2.4.4-A.2.4.5; explicit mapping-space proof of the fibrant-object alternative, using the path-object constant section.
